title: Production-grade phase prompts: groom and split
description:
## Goal
Replace the stub-grade groom and split prompts (prompts/phases/groom.md, split.md) with production prompts, as called out in AGENTS.md: prompts are stub-grade by design until M4.

## Scope
Design each prompt around its output contract (fenced ```json verdict blocks parsed by extractVerdict/validateVerdict). Groom must classify tickets: ready, needs-info, or blocked, with a human-readable reason and a confidence score low enough to trigger the council when warranted. Split must emit subtask decomposition only for genuinely multi-part work, each subtask independently deliverable and testable. Both prompts must respect the context firewall: they never see conductor state, other phases' context, or vendor vocabulary. Reference the existing ticket fixture shape in examples/polish-law/tickets.json for realistic input.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Verdict fixtures for each phase cover: happy path, low confidence (council escalation), malformed JSON (VerdictParseError path), and empty input.
2. test/verdict.spec.ts extended with cases derived from the new prompt contracts; all pass offline.
3. Firewall test still passes: groom/split inputs are assembled only in their input() functions.
4. Each prompt documents its inputs, output contract, and failure modes in a header comment.
5. pnpm test and pnpm typecheck pass.

## Out of scope
Execute/review/test prompts (WHIP-2), runtime changes, new phases.

title: Production-grade phase prompts: execute, review, test
description:
## Goal
Replace the stub execute, review, and test prompts with production prompts that make the conductor's bounded loops genuinely useful (M4, part 2).

## Scope
Execute: worktree-aware implementation prompt that reads the ticket and plan artifacts only, and emits a structured completion verdict. Review: fresh-context review (never sees plan/council/execution context — firewall) emitting findings with severity and a verdict that the executor-review loop can act on within budget.maxLoopRounds. Test: acceptance-criteria-driven test authoring prompt producing runnable tests. All three must keep the executor-review loop bounded and escalate stalemates to the ticket, as enforced in conductor code.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Loop integration tests (test/loop.spec.ts) extended: converge on round 2 with the new prompt contracts; stalemate escalates after maxLoopRounds.
2. Firewall test extended to cover the review phase's isolation.
3. Verdict fixtures cover low-confidence review, malformed verdicts, and empty output.
4. pnpm test and pnpm typecheck pass.

## Out of scope
Groom/split prompts (WHIP-1), budget changes, runtime changes.

title: whipper doctor: one-shot preflight for adapters and keys
description:
## Goal
Add `whipper doctor` — a read-only preflight that tells a new user exactly what is missing before any run, because right now misconfiguration only surfaces as runtime errors deep in a crack.

## Scope
Check and report, with ✅/❌ per item: config discovery and round-trip load; tracker adapter reachability (discoverWorkspace for linear/linear-mcp; note when fake); codehost adapter (gh auth status for github); model classes resolvable via resolveModel against the runtime catalog; ledger directory writable; worktrees directory usable (git worktree add/remove dry). Doctor never mutates the tracker, never opens PRs, and works fully offline with fake adapters. JSON output mode via --json.

## Acceptance criteria
1. whipper doctor in an all-fake repo with a valid config exits 0 and lists every check as ✅ or n/a (fake).
2. Missing LINEAR_API_KEY with the linear adapter produces a precise, actionable ❌ line including the .env.example hint.
3. Unknown model class in agents.*.model is reported with the exact agent role and class name.
4. Exit code is 1 when any required check fails, 0 otherwise; --json emits machine-readable results.
5. Help entry appears in the CLI (whipper doctor --help) and README documents it in the FIRST RIDE section.
6. pnpm test covers doctor's report building as a pure function; typecheck passes.

## Out of scope
Vercel/preview checks, fixing detected problems, interactive repair.

title: Close M3: real target-repo PR published by the conductor
description:
## Goal
AGENTS.md is explicit: a real deployed target-repo PR is still required to close M3. Run the conductor against a real throwaway target repo and land a real PR end to end.

## Scope
Prerequisites: gh auth login, a real model key in opencode user config, a scratch target repo with .whipper/config.json (linear or fake tracker, github codehost, opencode runtime). Run whipper crack on one ticket; let the publish phase open the PR; observe the GitHub checks and (if configured) the Vercel preview observation loop. Record the run in the ledger and capture the PR URL as evidence. File any adapter-shape drift discovered during the run as follow-up tickets instead of expanding this one.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A real PR exists on the target repo, opened by the conductor, containing only the executor's intended change (scratch-dir hygiene holds: no .opencode/, .whipper/ files committed).
2. The ledger (whipper ledger) shows the run's per-phase model usage.
3. If preview config is present, the await-preview phase observed a real deployment or recorded a precise reason it could not.
4. README 'For real' walkthrough is verified against this run and corrected where it drifted.
5. Any discovered drift is captured as new tickets with repro steps.

## Out of scope
New features in the conductor; prompt work (WHIP-1/WHIP-2).
